business_problem: Soul's AI-heavy social platform relied on virtual-machine deployments that made model development, release, and operations slow and repetitive. Engineers had to spend too much time on GPU drivers, CUDA environments, OSS data access, and fragmented infrastructure instead of improving matching, OCR, multimodal, and chatbot features.
solution_summary: Soul rebuilt its AI delivery layer on Alibaba Cloud Container Service for Kubernetes (ACK) Cloud-Native AI Suite to create a unified internal AI PaaS. The platform covers the full model lifecycle from data management to job release and model evaluation, which gives AI teams one operating surface instead of many ad hoc VM-based pipelines. Unified heterogeneous-resource management automates GPU node handling, separates algorithm code from standard images, and uses auto-scaling inference services so teams can deploy and operate models without repeatedly hand-tuning low-level infrastructure. Soul also uses GPU-sharing mechanisms and Fluid data acceleration to make large AI datasets easier to feed into workloads and to raise resource utilization across the fleet. In practice, the platform has grown from tens of GPUs to nearly a thousand while supporting voice matching, chatbots, OCR, image recognition, and other social-product AI services.
products_used: Container Service for Kubernetes (ACK) Cloud-Native AI Suite

solution_components.role: Accelerates data access for AI workloads so datasets can be reused more efficiently.

solution_components.name: GPU cloud servers
solution_components.role: Provide accelerated compute for the social platform's AI model workloads.

solution_components.name: Object Storage Service (OSS)
solution_components.role: Acts as the shared data source that previously required repetitive environment setup.

data_flow: Training data and model assets are stored in OSS-backed datasets and accelerated through Fluid, while ACK Cloud-Native AI Suite manages job submission, evaluation, deployment, and inference scaling. AI services such as voice matching, chatbots, OCR, and multimodal workloads then run on shared GPU fleets through the unified platform.
business_outcome: Soul converted fragmented AI engineering into a common internal platform, which sped releases, reduced repeated infrastructure work, and improved GPU utilization enough to lower cost materially. The company can now support far larger AI fleets and much higher deployment frequency without expanding operations effort at the same rate.

The same platform supports heterogeneous social-product AI scenarios rather than a single model type.
